_comment: Government policy positions a party's platform resolves to. One entry per field; a field's bands are read against a -100..100 axis and the first band whose range contains the value is the policy that party would enact. 'axis' names the platform axis it is read from; 'science' has no axis of its own and is derived (see NPCPolitics.policyAxes). Text is English only by design: these are data labels, not prose.

bands.name: Command economy
bands.desc: Every factory, farm and shop is planned and owned by the state.

bands.name: Public ownership
bands.desc: The commanding heights are nationalised; small trade is left alone.

bands.name: Social market
bands.desc: Private business under heavy taxation and a broad welfare floor.

bands.name: Mixed economy
bands.desc: A balanced budget, a mid tax rate and no strong doctrine either way.

bands.name: Market liberalism
bands.desc: Low tariffs, light regulation and a thin safety net.

bands.name: Deregulation
bands.desc: State industry sold off, labour law rolled back, capital untaxed.

bands.name: Laissez faire
bands.desc: The state collects almost nothing and guarantees almost nothing.

bands.name: Revealed truth
bands.desc: Inquiry is subordinate to doctrine; heterodox research is suppressed.

bands.name: Traditional learning
bands.desc: Schooling preserves the canon; new fields wait for permission.

bands.name: Applied research
bands.desc: Funding follows industry and defence, rarely curiosity.

bands.name: Public universities
bands.desc: Ordinary state funding for schools, faculties and journals.

bands.name: Research state
bands.desc: Laboratories, grants and technical schools are a budget priority.

bands.name: Technocratic planning
bands.desc: Policy is written by expert boards and audited against evidence.

bands.name: Scientific mandate
bands.desc: The academy sits in government; every ministry answers to review.

bands.name: Radical reform
bands.desc: Old institutions dissolved outright; customs are legislated against.

bands.name: Progressive reform
bands.desc: Rights extended fast, religious privilege dismantled.

bands.name: Secular civic order
bands.desc: A neutral state, no official creed, reform by ordinary majority.

bands.name: Civic balance
bands.desc: Neither restoration nor reform; the settlement stands as it is.

bands.name: Cultural conservatism
bands.desc: Family, church and custom are written into law and funded.

bands.name: Restorationism
bands.desc: Old ranks, offices and calendars are deliberately brought back.

bands.name: Sacred order
bands.desc: Custom is law; deviation from it is prosecuted.

bands.name: Disarmament
bands.desc: Standing forces abolished; weapons production is illegal.

bands.name: Pacifism
bands.desc: A token defence force and a constitutional bar on foreign war.

bands.name: Defensive posture
bands.desc: A small professional army held strictly for home defence.

bands.name: Standing army
bands.desc: An ordinary peacetime force, ordinary spending, no doctrine.

bands.name: Rearmament
bands.desc: Budgets rising, reserves called up, industry retooling.

bands.name: Conscription state
bands.desc: Universal service, a war economy and a garrisoned border.

bands.name: Total mobilisation
bands.desc: Every institution is organised around the next campaign.

bands.name: Militant rationalism
bands.desc: Occult practice is banned and its practitioners prosecuted.

bands.name: State secularism
bands.desc: No public money and no legal standing for the arcane.

bands.name: Regulated practice
bands.desc: Arcane work is licensed, taxed and kept out of government.

bands.name: Tolerated practice
bands.desc: The state neither funds the arcane nor moves against it.

bands.name: Chartered orders
bands.desc: Guilds and covens hold charters, seats and public contracts.

bands.name: Arcane establishment
bands.desc: An official cult, a state college of magic, sworn officials.

bands.name: Theurgic rule
bands.desc: Government is a liturgy; the rite decides what the ministry does.
